## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

According to its opening frame narrative, the Buddha recounted the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a certain monk who lived in a forest near a border village in the Kosala country after receiving meditation instructions from the Master. The past narrative concerns the virtue of frugality and features an exchange between Sakka and the parrot [Burlingame 1921].
